title: Hosted API GPU exhaustion postmortem and remediation action list
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-09 between 02:10-02:55 UTC the Hosted API experienced sustained request queue growth and abrupt throttling resulting in elevated 5xx rates and request latency for a subset of customers. Root cause: an interaction between the new autoscaler scroll-window heuristic and the soft GPU pool cap caused the serving fleet to stop provisioning additional GPUs for ~40 minutes. When the system hit the soft cap, request queueing increased; an unrelated change to the API throttling policy then triggered aggressive per-customer throttles instead of graceful fallbacks, amplifying customer-visible errors.

Timeline & detection: Alerts from the latency SLO pipeline fired at 02:18 UTC. On-call opened a P1 incident at 02:22. Manual scaling and temporary policy rollback were applied at 02:39 (mitigation 1) and full autoscaler rollback and config revert at 02:50. Incident declared resolved at 02:55 UTC. Root-cause analysis completed during post-incident review on 2026-03-11.

Impact: ~8% of traffic experienced >2s tail latency and ~1.2% of requests returned 5xx. No data loss. Affected customers were mainly medium-to-large hosted API tenants with concurrent long-context requests.

Immediate mitigations taken during incident:
- Rolled back autoscaler heuristic (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4298) by 02:39 UTC.
- Reverted throttling policy change and re-enabled graceful fallback to compatible model variants by 02:50 UTC.
- Manually increased GPU pool soft cap for the affected region for 3 hours.

Action items (owners and target dates):
1) Autoscaler fix: Harden the scroll-window heuristic to respect soft cap headroom and add backpressure signals from queue depth. Owner: Miguel Torres. Due: 2026-03-21. Subtask: ENG-10458.
2) Throttle policy rollback safety guard: Add an automated circuit-breaker that prevents aggressive per-customer throttles when queue depth trend is increasing. Owner: Priya Desai. Due: 2026-03-18. Subtask: ENG-10459.
3) Capacity playbook & runbook updates: Document step-by-step scaling and rollback procedures, include checklist for temporarily raising soft caps and communicating to Sales/CS. Owner: Jenna Park. Due: 2026-03-17. Subtask: ENG-10460.
4) Observability: Add a derived metric for 'GPU pool headroom' and an SLO alert that triggers when headroom drops below 10% for >5 minutes. Owner: Observability team. Due: 2026-03-16.
5) Post-deploy canary: For future autoscaler and throttling policy changes, require a regional canary (5% traffic) for 2 hours with automatic rollback on error rate regression. Owner: Runtime release leads. Due: 2026-03-25.

Verification & success criteria:
- Autoscaler change is validated in staging and rolled to canary with zero regression for 48h before region-wide rollout.
- Headroom alert fires in synthetic tests and the on-call runbook successfully remediates by following documented steps.
- Customer error rate for hosted API returns to baseline; we track 14-day rolling avg and require <0.2% regression.

Follow-ups and monitoring:
- Weekly incident review for 3 weeks to confirm no recurrence.
- Post-deploy dashboards: add 'queue depth per region', 'throttles by policy', and 'GPU pool headroom' to the runtime on-call dashboard.
- Notify impacted customers with a short incident summary and remediation notes; Sales/CS action: outreach completed by 2026-03-15.

Notes and artifacts:
- Full RCA doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INC-2026-03-09-gpu-exhaustion
- Incident timeline notes & Slack transcript: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0123456789/p1678451234000200
- Related PRs: autoscaler rollback https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4298, throttling rollback https://github.com/redwood-inference/api/pull/812

Open decisions:
- Whether to increase default soft cap headroom from 10% to 20% for peak-aware customers (pm review scheduled 2026-03-18).
- Whether to implement per-tenant burst tokens as an alternative to raising global soft caps.

Please tag any stakeholders on changes to autoscaler or throttling policy. This ticket will remain open until ENG-10458/ENG-10459/ENG-10460 are merged, validated in canary, and corresponding dashboard alerts are in place.
